summary: RBAC v2: Formalize break-glass procedure + required alerting updates for on-call workflows
description:
Requester (SRE): Rafael Mendes
Primary owner: Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Security partner: Marcus Lin
Eng partner: Kaitlyn Nguyen

Context
RBAC v2 rollout introduces time-bounded elevated sessions ("break-glass") and support/ops actions now returning explicit 403s when not permitted. SRE needs a formalized, auditable procedure that matches incident-time realities and satisfies Security/GRC expectations. Current process is a mix of tribal knowledge + ad-hoc approvals in Slack, with inconsistent alerting and incomplete evidence capture.

Problem statement
During incidents, on-call may need elevated permissions to:
- execute mitigation actions in control plane admin tooling (e.g., disable misbehaving rollout, adjust Dedicated pool scaling, suspend abusive API key)
- access customer org configuration read-only for diagnosis (support-like workflows)

Today:
- Approvals vary by incident commander
- Elevated access duration is not consistently enforced
- Alerting on break-glass usage is inconsistent (some events are only visible in audit logs after the fact)
- Post-incident evidence collection is manual

Request / scope
1) Formalize break-glass procedure as a single runbook that SRE can follow during incidents:
   - when break-glass is allowed vs not allowed
   - who can approve and how approvals are recorded
   - max duration and renewal rules
   - what actions are allowed during elevated session
   - mandatory post-use notes

2) Alerting updates:
   - Real-time alert in #incidents + #eng-security when break-glass is granted and when used for privileged operations
   - Separate alert when an elevated session exceeds TTL / renewal occurs
   - Daily/weekly digest for Security review (optional but preferred)

3) Evidence requirements for audits/security reviews:
   - authorization decision context in audit events (actor, role_ids, policy_version, decision, reason)
   - explicit "break_glass_granted" and "break_glass_revoked/expired" audit events
   - linkage to incident ID where applicable

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence runbook is updated and approved by Security (Marcus Lin) and SRE lead (Sean Gallagher)
- Alert routes are live in prod and validated via staging drill
- Audit events include required fields and can be exported without manual enrichment
- On-call training note posted to #eng-sre with a short checklist

Notes / constraints
- Must support Dedicated + Private customers without requiring broad Support impersonation.
- Break-glass should be time-bounded by default (target 30 minutes) with explicit renewal.
- Must not block incident response due to brittle tooling; have a fallback documented.

References
- Slack discussion (break-glass design): sources/slack/eng-security/thread_1739021144_552100.json
- Slack discussion (incident-time requirements): sources/slack/eng-sre/thread_1739169921_081223.json
- Runbook/policy baseline: sources/confluence/policies-and-process/access-and-permissions/support-break-glass-access.json
comments: 2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): We had two recent staging drills where we lost ~10–15 minutes figuring out who can approve and how to grant the elevated session. Requesting a single, incident-friendly runbook + automatic alerting. Also want clarity: does SRE break-glass imply support impersonation? (prefer no).

2025-02-19 (Sean Gallagher): Ack. Creating a concrete checklist + alerting requirements. Will coordinate with Marcus (Security) and Kaitlyn (authz implementation). We should treat this as a P1 since it affects incident response and auditability.

2025-02-19 (Marcus Lin): Agree. Requirements from Security side: (1) time-bounded grant; (2) approvals recorded outside Slack-only (audit log + ticket reference); (3) alert on grant + first privileged use; (4) deny-by-default for impersonation in Private deployments unless explicitly enabled by customer contract/policy.

2025-02-20 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implementation update: PR in flight for time-bounded elevated session plumbing w/ explicit audit events. We can add a webhook sink for alerts from the audit-log-exporter or from control plane audit pipeline. Need confirmation on channels + payload format.

2025-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): Proposed alerting:
- PagerDuty event (low urgency) + Slack message to #incidents and #eng-security on grant
- Slack message on revoke/expire
- Slack message on renewal
- Optional: message on first privileged operation under elevated session (to reduce spam)

Open question: do we alert on every privileged action? My preference is no; we should log everything but only alert on session lifecycle + first use.

2025-02-24 (Kevin Osei): From audit logging: we can include authz decision fields + break-glass session_id on privileged events. For alerting on "first privileged use", we can emit a derived event (break_glass_first_use) from the audit pipeline with a 1h de-dupe keyed by session_id.

2025-02-25 (Connor O'Brien): Please include a rollout plan + how to test in staging without granting global admin. We can run a controlled drill using a staging org and validate alert delivery + expiration handling. Also, add a note for release coordination since RBAC v2 flags are changing weekly.

2025-02-27 (Sean Gallagher): Draft runbook updates posted (link in Related Confluence). Includes: approval matrix (IC + Security on-call), 30-min TTL default, renewals max 2x, mandatory incident ID/INT ticket reference in the grant reason, and explicit prohibition on "support impersonation" unless customer allows (Private). Please review.

2025-02-28 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed and approved with one change: add a requirement that any break-glass use triggers a post-incident access review item (who/what/why). Also add explicit note: granting break-glass is separate from granting data access; prefer least privilege and scoped actions.

2025-03-01 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): PR merged for break-glass workflow plumbing + audit events. Follow-up PR will add dedupe alert derived event. For now we can alert on grant/revoke directly from audit events. (See related PR list.)

2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Staging drill completed. Alerts delivered to #incidents and #eng-security within ~15s of grant. Expiration alert fired at TTL. Renewal alert fired. Confirmed audit event contains actor, role_ids, policy_version, session_id, incident_id field populated when provided. Posting training note to #eng-sre and updating on-call handbook references.

2025-03-04 (Sean Gallagher): Marking Resolved. Follow-ups:
1) Add break_glass_first_use derived event (Kevin) to reduce noise while still getting a strong signal.
2) Add weekly digest to Security (optional).
3) Ensure Private deployments doc explicitly states default behavior re: impersonation (Elliot/Kira).
resolution: Runbook updated and approved; break-glass time-bounded procedure standardized; alerting on grant/revoke/expire/renewal validated in staging and enabled in prod. Audit events include required authz decision context + break-glass session identifiers. On-call training note posted and references updated.
next_steps: Implement optional break_glass_first_use derived alert; add weekly digest; confirm Private docs clarify impersonation default/opt-in; verify exporter mapping for new break-glass fields in SIEM targets.
